title: What Is Your Love Language?
description: Discover how you give and receive love. Based on the five love languages framework, this quiz reveals whether you're driven by words of affirmation, acts of service, receiving gifts, quality time, or physical touch. Answer 12 questions and find out which love language speaks to your heart.

questions.text: What makes you feel most loved in a relationship?

options.text: When my partner tells me how much they love and appreciate me.
When my partner does something helpful without being asked.
When my partner gives me a meaningful, thoughtful gift.
When my partner gives me their full, undivided attention.
When my partner holds my hand, hugs me, or sits close to me.

questions.text: It's your birthday. Which gift means the most to you?

options.text: A heartfelt handwritten letter expressing how much I mean to them.
They planned an entire day just for us — thoughtfully organized.
A thoughtful physical gift they knew I had been wanting.
They cooked my favorite meal from scratch.
A long, warm hug and spending the whole day cuddled together.

questions.text: After a tough day, what do you need most from your partner?

options.text: To hear them say 'I'm proud of you' or 'You've got this.'
For them to take something off my plate — cook, clean, or run an errand.
A small surprise — even flowers or my favorite snack — to lift my mood.
To sit together quietly or talk with no distractions.
A long hug or for them to hold me close without saying anything.

questions.text: You're away from your partner for a week. What do you miss most?

options.text: Their voice saying 'I love you' or kind, encouraging messages.
The little things they do for me every day without being asked.
Receiving a care package or a small gift in the mail from them.
Being in the same room with them, doing anything together.
Their physical presence — hugs, touch, just being close.

questions.text: How do you usually show love to others?

options.text: I tell them exactly how much they mean to me with words.
I help them out — I take action to make their life easier.
I find thoughtful gifts that remind me of them.
I carve out dedicated, distraction-free time just for them.
I hug them, hold their hand, or offer a reassuring touch.

questions.text: What small daily gesture means the most to you?

options.text: A good morning text or a 'thinking of you' message during the day.
My partner making coffee, handling a chore, or doing something helpful.
A small surprise — a chocolate, a flower, or something they picked up for me.
Having dinner together with no phones — fully present.
A spontaneous hug, a kiss on the forehead, or a hand on my shoulder.

questions.text: You feel disconnected from your partner. What would help most?

options.text: Having a heartfelt conversation where they express how they feel about me.
Them doing something thoughtful and practical to show they care.
A surprise gift — even small — to remind me they're thinking of me.
Spending quality time together with no distractions or interruptions.
Physical closeness — sitting together, a hug, or just holding hands.

questions.text: Your partner surprises you. Which surprise feels best?

options.text: A voice note or card telling me exactly why they love me.
They handled something I was stressed about — a task or errand.
A beautifully wrapped gift they chose just for me.
They planned a special day out — just the two of us.
They showed up just to be with me and hold me close.

questions.text: In an argument, what helps you feel resolved?

options.text: Hearing them apologize sincerely and say how much they value us.
Them doing something tangible to show me they want to make it right.
A peace offering — a small gesture or gift to break the tension.
Sitting down calmly and talking it through, fully present with each other.
A genuine hug — physical reconnection that says everything is okay.

questions.text: What do you most wish your partner did more often?

options.text: Told me they appreciate me, love me, and are proud of me.
Stepped up and helped more without me having to ask.
Surprised me with little gifts or tokens of their affection.
Put down their phone and was fully present with me.
Initiated physical affection — hugs, kisses, sitting close.

questions.text: You feel truly seen when your partner...

options.text: Compliments me, encourages me, and tells me they believe in me.
Goes out of their way to make my day easier without being asked.
Remembers something I mentioned and surprises me with a thoughtful gift.
Turns off distractions and gives me their complete attention.
Reaches for my hand or pulls me close without saying a word.

questions.text: If you could have more of one thing in your relationship, it would be...

options.text: More words of love, appreciation, and verbal encouragement.
More help and effort — my partner showing love through action.
More thoughtful surprises and tokens of affection.
More dedicated time together with no distractions.
More physical affection — touch, closeness, and warmth.

results.title: Words of Affirmation
results.description: Your love language is Words of Affirmation — you feel most loved and valued when the people you care about express their feelings openly and verbally. Compliments, encouragement, heartfelt messages, and hearing 'I love you' are not just nice to hear; for you, they are essential. You notice when partners make an effort to articulate their feelings, and you remember those words long after the moment has passed. Silence or withheld praise can feel like distance, even when nothing is wrong. You are likely an expressive communicator yourself — someone who naturally tells others what you love about them and lifts the people around you with sincere, specific words. In relationships, you thrive when your partner checks in verbally, leaves notes, sends thoughtful messages, or simply takes a moment to say what you mean to them. The right words from the right person can carry you through difficult times and make ordinary moments feel truly special.

results.title: Acts of Service
results.description: Your love language is Acts of Service — you feel most cared for when the people you love show up for you through action. When someone does the dishes without being asked, handles an errand you forgot, or takes care of a task that was weighing on you, that is love made tangible. You pay close attention to effort and follow-through, and you notice when people invest their time and energy to make your life better. For you, actions genuinely speak louder than words. You likely show love the same way — rolling up your sleeves and doing things for the people who matter to you without expecting credit. In relationships, you flourish when your partner is proactive, attentive, and willing to contribute practically to shared life. Being met halfway — or more — fills you with warmth and makes you feel deeply supported. The greatest gift someone can give you is their time and effort, willingly and lovingly given.

results.title: Receiving Gifts
results.description: Your love language is Receiving Gifts — and before you think this is about materialism, it's really about something much deeper: thoughtfulness. When someone gives you a gift, what moves you isn't the price tag — it's the fact that they were thinking of you when you weren't there. A wildflower picked on a walk, a book recommended because it reminded them of something you said, a small treat left on your desk — these tokens tell you that you are seen, remembered, and cherished. You are likely a highly sentimental person who keeps meaningful mementos and pays attention to what matters to others. You probably give extraordinarily thoughtful gifts yourself because you understand the emotional weight they carry. In relationships, you feel most loved when partners pay attention to what you mention, remember the details, and occasionally surprise you with something that says, quietly and clearly: I thought of you today.

results.title: Quality Time
results.description: Your love language is Quality Time — you feel most loved when someone gives you their undivided, present attention. Not just being in the same room, but truly being there: no phones, no half-listening, no multitasking. When someone carves out time specifically for you and brings their whole self to the moment, you feel deeply valued. A long walk together, a dinner with no distractions, or a quiet evening side by side doing something you both love — these are the things that fill your emotional tank. You likely have a gift for being genuinely present yourself, and you notice when others are mentally elsewhere even while physically with you. In relationships, your greatest need is for a partner who shows up fully — who prioritizes time with you and makes it clear, through their attention, that you matter. Quality always outweighs quantity, but for you, both genuinely matter.

results.title: Physical Touch
results.description: Your love language is Physical Touch — for you, physical presence and closeness are the most direct expression of love and safety. A hand on your shoulder, a spontaneous hug, holding hands while walking, or simply sitting close enough to touch — these moments tell you, without words, that you are loved and not alone. You are likely an affectionate person by nature, someone who reaches out naturally when someone you care about is hurting or celebrating. Physical disconnection can feel like emotional distance, even when everything else seems fine. You don't need grand gestures — a gentle touch at the right moment communicates more than a thousand words. In relationships, you thrive with a partner who is physically warm and affectionate, who gravitates toward closeness and understands that a hug is sometimes the most eloquent thing they can offer. Warmth, presence, and physical connection are the foundation of your deepest bonds.
